ScopeItemStatement: v1 is reached only when the D-GOV-21 §6 sequence has closed through step 9 - root packages materialized from an accepted root decomposition with G0-G4 registered and passing.
Notes: Materialization itself remains behind the D-GOV-21 §5.3 gate. Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: v1 requires the root product's own governed loop to have carried at least one complete deliverable stream end to end.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: v1 requires at least one situated working root operating on the same instruction basis with a recorded convergence path.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: Completeness is claimed only for the stated v1 boundary; if the owner defines v1 differently the success conditions re-scope accordingly.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: Objectives are objectives of the product rather than of any single tranche, and objectives unmapped at decomposition time are surfaced as open issues rather than silently dropped.

v1 targets the present owner-practitioner on a staged trajectory toward individual professional knowledge workers generally and then multi-practitioner organizations, and that trajectory is what keeps the discoverability condition non-trivial at v1.
The B and C stages of the ruled user-scope trajectory are declared trajectory, not v1 scope.
Notes: Boundary item; carried so later work cannot silently pull B/C obligations into v1.

ScopeItemStatement: The root product is constituted by four functional categories - normative basis, operative product, developmental machinery, and evidence.
The categories are related by a generative loop whose closing step - human judgment - no agent can perform.
Notes: Cross-package deliverable mapping: the loop's evidence-to-evaluation arc is instrumented by the evidence package.

ScopeItemStatement: The single human-judgment step resolves into three judgments that must not be collapsed: evaluation of the work, iteration on the product, and the release lifecycle judgment.
Notes: Release is separately gated at §8.3 and owned by DEL-06-07.

ScopeItemStatement: Deterministic tools, guards, and validators supply findings to the three judgments and gate objective preconditions; they never perform any of the judgments.
The categories classify functions and authority relationships, are non-exclusive, and do not prescribe four packages; the decomposition partition is not determined by them.
Dynamic registries are incorporated by reference rather than restated; where a live registry and a narrative list disagree, the live registry governs and the discrepancy is surfaced.

For authoritative governance and project-coordination state the substrate is git-tracked plain files; no external database, server state, or configuration holds that truth, rebuildable projections are permitted and never citable as authority, and a decision not in a versioned file does not exist for reliance.
Notes: Split from the stated domain-engine exception, which is SOW-015.

ScopeItemStatement: Domain engines own authoritative domain truth and are exempt from the rebuildable-projection rule; the product governs the work around the engine and is never the solver or the source of accepted engineering truth.
Notes: Split from N-1 because its maintenance locus is the variant/domain boundary.

ScopeItemStatement: The invariant catalog is the binding constraint set the product must continue to satisfy; it governs its own membership and no parallel invariant list is maintained.

Human authority holds at every consequential gate: only humans author binding approvals, approvals bind to a specific git SHA and are voided by content change, approvals are always and only binding, gates are dynamic per project with a stated minimum, and no machine BLOCK on the issuance judgment is non-overridable.

Epistemic discipline is architectural rather than advisory: mandatory provenance, unknowns become TBD rather than guesses, conflicts are surfaced with pointers rather than silently resolved, and claims are calibrated to their warrant.
Every agent has an explicit declared write scope.
Notes: N-5 split across its three enforcement loci (SOW-019, SOW-020, SOW-021).

ScopeItemStatement: Every scope path and write target resolves under the active checkout or the task stops.
Task outputs to tool roots are immutable snapshots.

The authority chain runs DIRECTIVE to CONTRACT to SPEC to TYPES with the live instruction surface alongside; where a lower or candidate document conflicts with ratified governance, ratified governance controls and the conflict is surfaced.
The four pillars - ontology, epistemology, praxiology, axiology - are the accountability ontology, and ontology, praxiology, and axiology exist to serve the epistemology.

The professional-responsibility model holds where it activates: AI outputs are drafts, the licensed professional retains scope, code selection, hazard acceptance, adjudication and issuance rights, competence includes tool competence, and the hierarchy of authority runs laws to codes to project specifications to verified analysis to professional judgment.
The normative basis is a constituent of the product rather than documentation about it: the requirement is that the running system continue to satisfy the invariants, not that it describe them.
The shared instruction surface is release-managed and read-mostly, and changing it is a repo-wide governance action rather than ordinary working-root execution.

The product operates through three layers with distinct authority boundaries: instruction artifacts carrying semantic authority contracts, deterministic tools producing facts and findings and never substituting for semantic judgment, and the runtime executable substrate whose transport never grants project authority and whose user-data state is operational rather than project truth.

The runtime delegation hierarchy is Agent 0 to Agent 1 to Agent 2 with declared entry rules, no delegation below Agent 2, and three Agent 2 construction forms; role membership is incorporated by reference to the live index.

Capability never confers authority: delegation implies no capability inheritance, a child's capability never becomes its parent's, and every child remains subject to sealed context, gate approval, path containment, enforced read/write scope, and durable evidence.
Method packs and deterministic operations are maintained as live registries, and the live registry is authoritative over any narrative list.
The path model defines two roots, one containment rule, and a closed root-token registry, and instruction, coordination, and plan files must not embed machine-absolute paths.
Governed work is structured as execution instances containing flat packages and deliverables with stable IDs, a canonical lifecycle state file, and human-triaged staleness propagation.

Deliverable-local dependency registers are authoritative and no central dependency graph is authoritative, while derived and aggregated graphs remain lawful coordination state including on-demand read-only aggregation and full-graph blocker computation.

The instruction root is separated from the working root with exactly one governed exception - the root product's working root is the repository root and root execution/ is its execution root, eligible for packages and deliverables only from an accepted root decomposition derived from an adopted PRD and only while the guards pass - and the replacement containment contract of mechanisms M1-M7 and guards G0-G4 with its gate ordering is required and incorporated by reference.

The operative product's boundary is exactly the three layers; no fourth machine execution substrate is claimed and none of the layers holds or grants project authority, which is why an instruction-surface change is a governance act rather than a code change.

A design change is carried by one of two terminal artifacts - it supersedes a decision record or arrives as PR review - never a new plan document; where the vehicle is a decision record it carries status, verbatim owner ruling, SHAs, date, framing, accepted basis, and record convention, with the register navigational and the per-decision records governing.

Within the two record classes where the convention governs - published decision records carrying the supersede-never-edit convention and ruled candidate packets bound to an accepted candidate SHA - corrections to ruled content are superseding acts rather than edits.
Notes: The broader change-control rule is carried separately at D-16.

ScopeItemStatement: Attribution of rulings and adoptions matches an owner-curated identity allowlist, identity-dependent checks refuse rather than guess, and the list is not extended programmatically.

Validation is deterministic and severity-typed with exit-code semantics and human-only recorded BLOCK override, BLOCK never means globally proven safe or unsafe, and a validator finding may never mechanically reject content the owner has ruled - where ruled text trips a validator, the validator is defective.

Phase-crossing work is bound by the governance integration rules - derivative-package, snapshot, handoff-state, closure, sequencing, cycle-resolution, and change-notice routing - incorporated by reference.

Root-product development runs through a governed loop with a session-init contract, a deterministic standing-plan pointer, and an append-only receipts log, and coordination surfaces carry no authority merely because they exist; on disagreement with a live source the live source governs and the delta is recorded.

Git closeout in every registered loop runs through the shared change-management role with human-gated pull requests as the standing default. Beyond that default, the owner may direct merge execution — typed by the owner directly or executed by an agent as the owner's proxy, identical authority either way — with the direction recorded in the loop's ordinary closeout evidence (approved source HEAD, owner direction, effective merge SHA), preserving K-MERGE-1. Each loop's stricter local merge discipline remains controlling until that loop adopts or acknowledges the policy under its own instruments.
The decomposition pipeline is not waivable: packages and deliverables come only from an accepted decomposition, and nothing authorizes inventing packages from discussion.

The public-export boundary is an explicit allowlist profile that copies allowlisted content, sanitizes private absolute paths, writes a manifest and report, and fails on forbidden paths or leaks; the profile is the boundary contract and is incorporated by reference.
A tranche changing surfaces that downstream loops pin or mirror ships a routed coordination notice to each affected loop in the same tranche, as coordination rather than authority.
Developmental machinery is product scope rather than surrounding process - a legitimate target of decomposition, deliverables, and acceptance rather than exempt overhead.
Once adopted the PRD is amended only by a superseding instrument bound to a git SHA; the adopted bytes are never overwritten at their path and each revision is a new attributable act.
Notes: Source label is PROPOSED; the adoption instrument records that the PROPOSED items take effect (OI-002). Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: An adopted PRD that incorporates accepted doctrine carries a standing source-currency check over nine declared classes, pairing the source-corpus basis with the containing commit of the adopted bytes; a currency failure is a REVIEW finding routed to the owner and never an automatic amendment.
Notes: Five classes are mechanical and four require semantic judgment. Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: The source-currency check is not built - no generator, schema, or executable check exists at the stated basis - and building it is a precondition of relying on it.
Notes: Open issue OI-005: reliance on D-14 before the build is unwarranted. Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: The first root decomposition demonstrates coverage across all four functional categories, each having decomposition coverage or a recorded reasoned deferral; this constrains coverage demonstration only and does not prescribe the partition.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: Any change to previously approved content requires a new attributable act bound to the resulting SHA with prior approved bytes recoverable in Git; only artifact classes explicitly declared immutable are never overwritten at their path, while living authoritative surfaces amend in place through accepted commits.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: Every orchestration run persists a durable versioned record tree capturing plan, work graph, briefs, returns, notices, dispositions, amendments, and final handoff state; run IDs are created only when a real run begins, and placeholder runs or briefs presented as executed children are prohibited.
Phase-boundary decisions terminate in immutable snapshots, stopping work emits an explicit handoff state, and each lawful tranche appends a minimal receipt.

The three SHA roles are distinct and recorded distinctly: the owner act binds approved content to its candidate SHA, the publication SHA identifies the durable ruling record, and the effective SHA identifies applied state.

Claims carry epistemic labels and progress through the warrant lifecycle, and authentication is an accountable actor's scoped, purpose-specific, SHA-bound act that neither creates knowledge nor establishes truth.
Read-only audit and evaluation surfaces exist and are governed, with membership incorporated by reference to the live agent index.

Validation evidence is written only under declared generated paths under the mutation-control contract, the harness never writes governed authority files, and governed-file mutation by a validation command is an unconditional BLOCK.

A scope unit or phase is not closed because files were written: closure requires accepted authoritative truth, regenerated or explicitly deferred derivatives, recorded audit status, and surfaced unresolved blockers.

Evidence completeness is not evidence sufficiency: the provenance ladder measures whether warrant is present, never whether it is adequate for a given reliance purpose, which is a human judgment against scope and purpose.

Self-application is operationalized by the ruled D-GOV-21 §6 sequence, whose later steps - PRD adoption, first root decomposition with Project Setup, and materialization behind the §5.3 gate - are individually gated.
Notes: OI-001: the PRD's step status statements pre-date later accepted acts at the current basis.

ScopeItemStatement: Until the materialization gate closes, root execution/ holds control-plane records only.
A root node may not consume a capability produced by root development before that capability was accepted through the basis or an explicitly accepted predecessor.
Deterministic guards and human gates supply containment but neither supplies authorization; the instruction-surface gate does not itself grant authorization.

The exact-candidate-SHA procedure is an observed practice exercised on substantial governance proposals rather than a governing rule; the actual invariant is that every approval binds to a specific git SHA, and vehicle selection is professional judgment.

Four accepted mechanisms make concurrent root development safe: fine-grained write ownership with disjoint or serialized targets, a frozen instruction basis per run, worktree isolation for concurrent children, and a pre-dispatch work-graph check validating declared and disjoint write targets.
Notes: The mechanisms' state surfaces are instantiated in PKG-03; this unit owns the concurrency-safety relation.

ScopeItemStatement: Legibility of concurrent work is a property of declared, file-recorded write ownership, so every active run's ownership and gates must remain reconstructible from coordination state and work graphs are recorded before dispatch rather than after.
One instruction root serves many working roots without per-workspace instruction drift.
A working root may extend the invariant catalog and may overlay or specialize the agent suite, but must not weaken framework governance.
No variant inherits the root working-root exception, and the exception extends to no other working root.
Variants specialize root patterns for particular forms of knowledge work.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: Observed friction and successful patterns in variants may return as evidence-linked root candidates.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: No variant automatically changes or weakens root; a pattern's success in a working root is evidence, not authority.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: Promotion occurs only through the root's human-governed developmental machinery - a candidate, a ruling, and an accepted tranche.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: No change to the public-export boundary.
Notes: Boundary item.

ScopeItemStatement: No extension of the root working-root exception to any other working root or to desktop-selected folders.
Notes: Boundary item.

ScopeItemStatement: No waiver of the decomposition pipeline.
Notes: Boundary item.

ScopeItemStatement: No blanket authority for future root-structure changes.
Notes: Boundary item.

ScopeItemStatement: No change to the named human-authority, binding, gate, and sealed-context invariants, or to any invariant or clause not named in the authorizing packet.
Notes: Boundary item.

ScopeItemStatement: The PRD is not a roadmap; the roadmap surface remains separate, and no packages, deliverables, acceptance tests, or priority rankings are introduced by the PRD itself.
Notes: Boundary item; also the reason this decomposition derives partition rather than inheriting one.

ScopeItemStatement: F1 - containment failure: root self-development corrupts a shared instruction surface out from under a situated loop in a way the superseded separation would have prevented, undetected and ungated by the containment mechanisms and guards.
F2 - loop bypass: root development proceeds outside the root governed loop, materialized without a current workplan pointer, receipts, and the governance machinery engaged.
F3 - self-authorization: a root node consumes a capability produced by root development before that capability was accepted.

F4 - requirements drift: at the close of the first root decomposition, an accepted scope unit cannot be traced to a PRD requirement or objective, or a PRD requirement or objective has neither coverage nor a recorded deferral.
Notes: This candidate's bidirectional traceability registers are the artifact F4 is checked against. Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: F5 - concordance failure: the adopted PRD and the ratified genus clause come to say incompatible things about what the root product is, without a recorded superseding act on one of them.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: F6 - label decay: a provenance label changes without a superseding instrument, or a PROPOSED item is relied upon as though adopted.
Notes: OI-002 records a live label-status question for owner ruling. Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: Release is a separately human-gated lifecycle judgment over whether the current product state may be released, drawing on both operative and developmental evidence and informed by validation results, decomposition coverage, and guard state, none of which releases the product mechanically or constitutes the judgment.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: Release is not an iteration decision: it asks whether what exists may go out, and may be negative with no change proposed or positive with changes pending.
Notes: Label effect: in effect per the D-GOV-22 adoption ruling; confirmed at the D-GOV-25 ruling (source label unchanged; F6 discipline — no label change without an instrument).

ScopeItemStatement: The ruled genus settles what the product is for this PRD and does not by itself amend any governance surface.
Obligation (a): supersede the ratified genus clause through an exact-prose, human-gated act, until which the ratified clause remains in force as written.
Notes: OI-001: an accepted act at the current basis appears to have discharged this; coverage is standing verification, not re-performance.

ScopeItemStatement: Obligation (b): reword the non-binding derivative top-level description to the ruled genus, as propagation rather than supersession.
Notes: OI-001 applies.

ScopeItemStatement: Obligation (c): survey the specification, vocabulary, and live-index prose that leans on the contained-level term and propagate where the ruled two-level formulation changes the sense; the survey's scope is its own output rather than assumed.
Notes: OI-001 applies.

ScopeItemStatement: Jurisdiction for v1 is a single root owner, and accountability is one accountable owner per root inherited by acts within it, with a declared scaling path that is expressly not current scope.
The identity allowlist stays owner-curated - additions and removals are owner edits published through change management and not extended programmatically.
The database-backed multi-practitioner attribution interface named in the ruled evolution path is expressly not current scope, and its referent is TBD in the source rather than guessed.
Notes: OI-009: TBD referent carried, not resolved.

ScopeItemStatement: The adoption instrument is a decision record on the exact-candidate-SHA pattern, and the concordance map it carries is bidirectional with uncovered items on either side marked TBD - the artifact the concordance falsifier is checked against.

Placement is a split with a pointer: the adopted bytes are placed on the doctrinal surface through the existing export allowlist with no boundary change, candidates and revision evidence remain immutable on the coordination surface, and future amendments are instruction-surface tranches.

The concordance annex is a derivative package and derived publication artifact - never itself adopted, never the amendment surface, specified for regeneration - and adoption binds the exact bytes of the main document only.

Conflict C-1 - the genus wording divergence between the ratified clause, the derivative top-level description, and the ruled genus - is resolved in principle with concordance pending and closes fully only when the concordance tranche lands.
Notes: OI-001: appears closed by an accepted act at the current basis.

ScopeItemStatement: Conflict C-2 - invariant-index arithmetic between the catalog's stated count and its defined membership - is carried with the owner's ruling outstanding and a correction tranche recommended.
Notes: OI-001: appears corrected at the current basis.

ScopeItemStatement: Conflict C-3 - the historical-note date bearing on owner testimony that no in-repo source can settle - is carried expressly for owner confirmation.
Notes: OI-001: recorded as confirmed and closed at the adoption ruling.

ScopeItemStatement: Conflict C-4 - the derivative export description omitting a directory the export profile allowlists - is carried as propagation with the live profile governing.
Notes: OI-001: appears corrected at the current basis.

ScopeItemStatement: Adoption requires the exact bytes bound at a named SHA, the bidirectional concordance map, and the owner ruling recorded verbatim and attributed to a matching registered actor; no agent act substitutes for any of these, and until adoption every PROPOSED item is inert while transcribed commitments remain in force on their own authority.
Notes: OI-002: the adoption instrument records that the PROPOSED items take effect; the source bytes still carry the PROPOSED label.

ScopeItemStatement: Adoption does not materialize anything under root execution/, does not create a root decomposition, and does not change the public-export boundary.
Notes: Boundary item; the present run is the decomposition candidate and accepts nothing.

ScopeItemStatement: Consequential work on generic runtime semantics uses a Root-owned standing scope carrier and declared runtime write locus; preserves the authority, security, residency, exclusion, and implementation-gate boundaries ruled by D-GOV-20; produces versioned-contract, affected-client conformance or migration, and proportionate regression evidence; returns release disposition to an accountable human; and does not transfer generic runtime ownership to App, PEC, or another client.
Notes: Standing carrier activated one bounded runtime-change tranche at a time. D-GOV-20 remains the ruled architectural basis; D-T0-23 is a coordinating Tier-0 counterpart, not a Root scope source. O-11 is in effect through D-GOV-28.
